_meta: The daily lift of a new feature over an experiment, used to show the NOVELTY EFFECT: when a feature launches, users engage with it out of curiosity, inflating the early metrics, and the effect DECAYS as the novelty wears off -- so a short experiment (or the average over a window that includes the novelty spike) overstates the true long-run effect. daily_lift is the measured lift (e.g. extra clicks per user) on each day of the experiment; it starts high (10 on day 1, pure novelty) and decays to a steady state of 3 by day 5, which persists. short_window_days is how many early days a rushed analysis would average. The trap: averaging the first 3 days gives a lift of 7.33, and even averaging ALL 8 days gives 4.75 -- both far above the true long-run lift of 3 -- because any average over a decaying curve is pulled up by the early novelty. The honest estimate of the long-run effect is the STEADY STATE (the plateau the lift decays to, here 3), reached by running the experiment long enough for novelty to wear off and reading the flat tail, not by averaging over the decay. Shipping decisions and forecasts based on the early or windowed average overstate the feature's lasting value. daily_lift and short_window_days are the fixture; the short-window mean, full-window mean, and steady-state estimate are computed.
